newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Paris stocks lifted to new peaks by US data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Paris stocks lifted to new peaks by US data.

text.p: Paris stocks hit record levels on Wednesday and other European bourses climbed, lifted by U.S. economic data which allayed fears of an interest rate increase in the near future.

In currencies, the American figures pointing to non-inflationary pressures had the opposite effect, causing the dollar to lose its early gains as the changed U.S. rate outlook made dollar assets less attractive to investors.

Paris put on a sparkling performance, soaring to an all-time high in morning trade. It was boosted by new opinion polls suggesting a big win for the centre-right government in upcoming elections. They then raced to new peaks in the afternoon as the U.S. figures hit trading screens.

The Washington data showed the biggest decline in producer prices in nearly four years in April, tumbling by 0.6 percent and tempering concerns that the inflation-wary U.S. central bank will raise interest rates at a meeting next Tuesday.
"It's obviously very good news," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp in New York as Wall Street opened and quickly climbed by 0.8 percent.

French investors, also encouraged by the better outlook for government parties regarded as more sympathetic to business, pushed the blue-chip CAC-40 index up two percent to a high of 2781.87 points, bettering the previous intra-day record set two months ago.
"All the signs are on green, the dollar, the bond market and the polls," a broker said.

A CSA poll on Tuesday night gave 317 seats to the centre-right majority against 215 to the Socialists and allies. This followed a BVA poll giving 303 to the majority and 226 to the Socialists and allies.
Jacques Chahine Finance has predicted that if the government parties win, fund managers belived the CAC would head above 3,000. If the Socialists win it could fall to 2,400.
But dealers said some factors could puncture the French euphoria.

Large fund inflows were currently fuelling the market as foreign funds take comfort from the polls and invest in France, which has been lagging behind other markets. But a poll showing a swing back to the Socialists could scare these investors away again.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks see-sawed after a record-breaking run which has seen the blue-chip FTSE 100 index climb 10 percent in the last four weeks.

By early afternoon and despite the strong Wall Street start, shares just slipped into the negative column after making healthy gains in early trade. But dealers said some consolidation was inevitable after the recent bull run.
"We won't see much selling pressure today. Very few people want to sell stock at the moment," one senior dealer said. "But market makers will mark down prices until the buyers step in again."
In Frankfurt, dealings on the computerised IBIS index climbed 0.9 percent on the strength of the lower-than-expected U.S. inflation figures.
But floor trade, which closed at a record level on Tuesday, ended before the U.S. data was issued and was showing losses of 0.4 percent at the finish.
Deutsche Telekom was a one of the main losers, following reports that the Bonn government might consider selling some its Telekom shares to help cut its budget deficit.
On currency markets, the dollar edged down against the mark as dealers digested the news that an anticipated increase in U.S. interest rates would not happen after all.
Earlier the U.S. curency had climbed by about a pfennig on hopes of higher rates.
The dollar had also been helped by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke who said told a Vienna conference: "It seems that a dollar rate at around 1.70 marks conforms with the real data."
His Bundesbank colleague Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher said later in Warsaw he also believed dollar/mark levels were good.
Elsewhere, sterling rallied against a generally weaker mark. It was at 2.7901 marks compared with 2.7687 in late trade on Tuesday.

The pound was stronger on Tuesday affter the Bank of England said the recent strength of sterling improved the inflation outlook this year but that another interest rate rise was likely to be necessary to keep a lid on prices.
STOCK PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 4.9 points at 4,686.10.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 49.51 points at 2,769.09.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed down 21.46 points at 3,573.69.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7029 marks compared with 1.6965 late in Europe on Tuesday and 118.60 yen versus 118.83.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $349.10 an ounce after closing at $348.05 in London on Tuesday. Silver was up two cents at $4.87.
